metadata.title: CISA SCuBA SharePoint Online and OneDrive (MS.SHAREPOINT) Baseline - all policies

controls.title: External sharing for SharePoint SHALL be limited to "Existing guests" or "Only people in your organization".

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: External sharing for SharePoint SHALL be limited to "Existing guests" or "Only people in your organization".

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Sharing information outside the organization via SharePoint increases the risk of unauthorized access. By limiting external sharing, administrators decrease the risk of access to information.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose:
1. Sign in to the **SharePoint admin center**.

2.  Select **Policies** \> **Sharing**.

3.  Adjust external sharing slider for SharePoint to **Existing guests** or **Only people in your organization**.

4. Select **Save**.

controls.title: External sharing for OneDrive SHALL be limited to "Existing guests" or "Only people in your organization".

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: External sharing for OneDrive SHALL be limited to "Existing guests" or "Only people in your organization".

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Sharing files outside the organization via OneDrive increases the risk of unauthorized access. By limiting external sharing, administrators decrease the risk of unauthorized access to information.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose:
1.  Sign in to the **SharePoint admin center**.

2.  Select **Policies** \> **Sharing**.

3.  Adjust external sharing slider for OneDrive to **Existing Guests** or **Only people in your organization**.

4. Select **Save**.

controls.title: External sharing SHALL be restricted to approved external domains and/or users in approved security groups per interagency collaboration needs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: External sharing SHALL be restricted to approved external domains and/or users in approved security groups per interagency collaboration needs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: By limiting sharing to domains or approved security groups used for interagency collaboration purposes, administrators can help prevent sharing with unknown organizations and individuals.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose:
Note: If SharePoint external sharing is set to its most restrictive setting of "Only people in your organization", then no external sharing is allowed and no implementation changes are required for this policy item.

1.  Sign in to the **SharePoint admin center**.

2.  Select **Policies** \> **Sharing**.

3.  Expand **More external sharing settings**.

4.  Select **Limit external sharing by domain**.

5.  Select **Add domains**.

6.  Add each approved external domain users are allowed to share files with.

7.  Select **Manage security groups**

8. Add each approved security group. Members of these groups will be allowed to share files externally.

9.  Select **Save**.

groups.title: File and Folder Default Sharing Settings

controls.title: File and folder default sharing scope SHALL be set to "Specific people (only the people the user specifies)".

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: File and folder default sharing scope SHALL be set to "Specific people (only the people the user specifies)".

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: By making the default sharing the most restrictive, administrators prevent accidentally sharing information too broadly.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose:
1.  Sign in to the **SharePoint admin center**.

2.  Select **Policies** \> **Sharing**

3.  Under **File and folder links**, set the default link type to **Specific people (only the people the user specifies)**

4.  Select **Save**

controls.title: File and folder default sharing permissions SHALL be set to view only.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: File and folder default sharing permissions SHALL be set to view only.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Edit access to files and folders could allow a user to make unauthorized changes.  By restricting default permissions to **View** only, administrators prevent unintended or malicious modification.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose:
1.  Sign in to the **SharePoint admin center**.

2. Select **Policies** \> **Sharing**.

3. Under **File and folder links**, set the permission that is selected by default for sharing links to **View**.

4. Select **Save**.

groups.title: Securing Anyone Links and Verification Code Users

controls.title: Expiration days for Anyone links SHALL be set to 30 days or less.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Expiration days for Anyone links SHALL be set to 30 days or less.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Links may be used to provide access to information for a short period of time. Without expiration, however, access is indefinite. By setting expiration timers for links, administrators can prevent unintended sustained access to the link.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose:
1.  Sign in to the **SharePoint admin center**.

2.  Select **Policies** \> **Sharing**.

3.  Scroll to the section **Choose expiration and permissions options for Anyone links**.

4.  Select the checkbox **These links must expire within this many days**.

5.  Enter **30** days or less.

6.  Select **Save**.

controls.title: The allowable file and folder permissions for links SHALL be set to view only.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The allowable file and folder permissions for links SHALL be set to view only.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Unauthorized changes to files can be made if permissions allow editing by anyone.  By restricting permissions on links to **View** only, administrators prevent anonymous file changes.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose:
1.  Sign in to the **SharePoint admin center**.

2.  Select **Policies** \> **Sharing**.

3.  Scroll to the section **Choose expiration and permissions options for Anyone links**.

4.  Set the configuration items in the section **These links can give these permissions**.

5.  Set the **Files** option to **View**.

6.  Set the **Folders** option to **View**.

7.  Select **Save**.

controls.title: Reauthentication days for people who use a verification code SHALL be set to 30 days or less.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Reauthentication days for people who use a verification code SHALL be set to 30 days or less.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: By setting expiration timers for verification code access, administrators can prevent unintended sustained access to documents.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose:
1.  Sign in to the **SharePoint admin center**.

2.  Select **Policies** \> **Sharing**.

3.  Expand **More external sharing settings**.

4. Select **People who use a verification code must reauthenticate after this many days**.

5.  Enter **30** days or less.

6. Select **Save**.
